newsitem.title: PERU: Peru govt has legislative powers extended 30 days.
newsitem.headline: Peru govt has legislative powers extended 30 days.

text.p: The Peruvian Congress granted Thursday a 30-day extension to the government's special legislative powers.
But it voted to shelve a separate request from the government for special powers to decree a new law governing the financial sector.
Congress' 120-member single chamber voted 54 to 20 to extend the government's period of special legislative powers, which was due to end September 28.
The vote to shelve the government's request to decree a financial sector law was unanimous.
In June, Congress granted the government special powers for 90 days to decree a wide range of political, economic and financial legislation.
Among the most important measures being drawn up by the government are laws to:
- Free prisoners wrongly jailed on terrorism charges.
- Create a commercial "corridor" in southern Peru.
- Update regulations covering the local stock market in order to unify the types of shares being traded.
- Update regulations covering the pension sector.
- Regulate property titles and facilitate credits to the agriculture sector.
Congress President Victor Joy Way said earlier this week the special powers were being granted only for detailed and complicated legislation, which required government experts.

Congress also voted Thursday to grant the government powers to decree the creation of a second commercial "corridor" along the country's northern coast linking the cities of Paita, Piura, Sullana and Tumbes.
